title: Villieria pricing: Essential Circuit Wiring, Priced per board split — the number of circuits moved drives the cost

If you are pricing Essential Circuit Wiring in Villieria, the number you want is Priced per board split — the number of circuits moved drives the cost. That is a band, not a promise — but it is a real band, published up front, and it is close enough to budget against.

How that number is derived: This is often the cheapest way to make a backup system work better, and it is routinely skipped. Splitting the board so backup feeds only what matters usually lets you buy a smaller inverter or generator, which saves more than the board work costs. We will show you that arithmetic before you buy equipment.

It is quoted per board, which matters: two quotes on different bases are not comparable, however similar the rand figure looks.

What we are actually talking about: Deciding what stays on is a design decision, and it is where backup budgets are won.

title: Springs homes and What an Aluminium Window Actually Costs: what the area actually needs
long:
Springs sits in Ekurhuleni/East Rand. An East Rand town with older freestanding houses, flats and townhouse developments, plus industrial areas.

Housing here is mostly older freestanding houses, flats and townhouses, which is exactly why What an Aluminium Window Actually Costs comes up as often as it does in this area.

The band for What an Aluminium Window Actually Costs is R350 – R800 per m² and R3,000 – R6,000 per window are both published — they describe different things. Quoted per m² | per unit. Both figures above come from published South African cost guides gathered November 2026. Work them through on a standard 1.5 m by 1.2 m window, which is 1.8 m². At R800 per m² that is R1,440. The per-window guide says R3,000 to R6,000 for the same thing. They cannot both describe a supplied and installed window. The reconciliation is that the per-square-metre figure describes labour or supply alone, while the per-unit figure describes the finished job. Nobody in this market explains that, and it is why every buyer thinks they are being overcharged.

We work the area around Springs Mall and the suburbs next to it.

What to check before booking in Springs:

- Get the glass thickness and whether it is toughened or laminated
- Ask whether removal, making good and sealing are included

How that number is derived: Four public sources gathered in November 2026 disagree by roughly double on the same job. A drilling-company city guide puts Roodepoort at R350–R650 and Centurion at R420–R750 per metre. A separate cost guide says R700–R1,200 with R950 typical. A June 2026 company announcement cites R900–R1,400. An industry body figure quoted in the press puts the average near R600. None of these is our rate card. The spread exists because sellers quote high, guides quote wide, and nobody states what is included — so ask every quote what the metre rate covers.

It is quoted per metre, which matters: two quotes on different bases are not comparable, however similar the rand figure looks.

Rivonia specifics. A northern Sandton suburb with large freestanding houses on large stands, townhouse complexes and office parks. Housing here is mostly large freestanding houses, townhouses and office parks, and that drives the final figure more than anything a call centre will tell you.

The reconciliation is that the per-square-metre figure describes labour or supply alone, while the per-unit figure describes the finished job. Nobody in this market explains that, and it is why every buyer thinks they are being overcharged.

If you are pricing Full House Renovation in Pretoria West, the number you want is Quoted per project — renovation rates vary far more than new-build rates. That is a band, not a promise — but it is a real band, published up front, and it is close enough to budget against.

How that number is derived: We will not publish a renovation rate per square metre, because unlike new build it means almost nothing. One published 2026 figure puts a mid-finish 22 square metre kitchen rebuild in Gauteng or the Cape at R600,000 to R750,000 — the same source warns that a R400,000 quote without a detailed bill of quantities is not comparable. That warning is the most useful sentence published in this market.

It is quoted per project, which matters: two quotes on different bases are not comparable, however similar the rand figure looks.

Pretoria West specifics. An older area west of the Pretoria city centre mixing freestanding houses, flats and light-industrial premises. Housing here is mostly older freestanding houses, flats and complexes, and that drives the final figure more than anything a call centre will tell you.

What we are actually talking about: Renovating a whole house, in an order that does not undo itself.

Where quotes go wrong

- Snag list agreed verbally and never written down
- No programme with weather days, so the overrun is automatic
- No NHBRC or council approval on work that needed it

What to confirm before you pay anything

- Tie payments to completed stages, never to dates
- Ask for the programme with weather days shown
- Agree the retention percentage held until the snag list closes
- Insist on a bill of quantities with the quote
- Confirm which drawings and council approvals are included

priceBand: Unit plus installation, quoted with the required pre-filtration included
title: "How much is UV Disinfection in Midstream Estate?" — a straight answer
long:
Short answer: Unit plus installation, quoted with the required pre-filtration included.

Long answer, because the short one hides the part that matters. The job is priced per installation. Always quoted with pre-filtration, because UV without it does not work and selling it that way is close to dishonest. Ultraviolet light has to reach the organism; turbid water shields bacteria from the lamp. A UV quote that does not include sediment filtration is incomplete.

Killing bacteria without chemicals, and the one thing UV cannot do.

In Midstream Estate specifically, the housing is mostly estate homes and townhouses, so the band tends to sit where you would expect rather than at either extreme.

The follow-up questions worth asking:

- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration
- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded
- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing
- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry

And the things that push a quote up unexpectedly: a pressure pump sized for the tap, not for the house; no first-flush diverter on a harvesting setup, so the tank collects roof grit.

long:
We get called out to the same Rainwater Harvesting problems over and over in Heidelberg. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. Drilling before a geohydrological siting report, then paying for a dry hole
2. A tank stand built for a full tank's weight only on paper
3. No first-flush diverter on a harvesting setup, so the tank collects roof grit

Each one of those turns a job of Quoted on roof area and storage, far below a borehole for most properties into a bigger one. For a great many Gauteng properties this is the honest first recommendation, and we would rather make the smaller sale. Harvesting is a fraction of a borehole's cost, needs no drilling risk and no groundwater registration. Its limit is that highveld rainfall is strongly seasonal — it will not carry you through a dry winter on its own, and we will say so before you buy.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded
- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing
- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry

title: The expensive mistake people make with Sand Filter Media Change
long:
We get called out to the same Sand Filter Media Change problems over and over in Waterkloof Ridge. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. A pump sized for the pipework someone else installed
2. Chasing chlorine when the real problem is pH and stabiliser
3. A weekly plan priced by phone call instead of by actual pool volume

Each one of those turns a job of Media plus labour, quoted per filter size into a bigger one. Priced on filter size, because that decides how much media goes in and how long the strip-down takes. Filter sand does not last forever — it rounds off, channels and clogs with oils, and then the filter physically cannot remove fine particles no matter how perfect the chemistry is.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Check what the visit actually covers, task by task

We get called out to the same Pool Pump Replacement problems over and over in Saxonwold. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. Chasing chlorine when the real problem is pH and stabiliser
2. A pump sized for the pipework someone else installed
3. Topping up a leak for a year instead of pressure-testing the lines

Each one of those turns a job of Pump plus installation, quoted as separate lines into a bigger one. We quote the pump and the installation separately so you can compare the equipment price against anyone else's and see exactly what the labour is. An oversized pump is the most common mistake in this trade: it costs more to buy, more to run, and can push water through a sand filter too fast to actually filter it.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Get the pump model and its rated flow against your filter
- Confirm whether chemicals are included or billed separately
- Check what the visit actually covers, task by task

priceBand: Quoted per box or per unit
title: The expensive mistake people make with Hardware and Fixings
long:
We get called out to the same Hardware and Fixings problems over and over in Northmead. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. No wastage allowance, then a second delivery fee for 40 bricks
2. Sand bought by the load with no idea of the cubic metres delivered
3. Ordering cement by the bag count instead of by the mix ratio

Each one of those turns a job of Quoted per box or per unit into a bigger one. Priced per box or unit. The two things that go wrong are substrate match and corrosion grade — a fixing rated for solid concrete behaves very differently in a hollow block, and a non-galvanised fastener outdoors on the highveld rusts and stains the wall below it within a season.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Ask what the delivery fee is per drop and per extra drop
- Check the cement strength class against the job
- Get the quantity schedule, not just a price per unit

long:

Each one of those turns a job of R350 – R750 per metre on Gauteng drilling-company guides, with other sources claiming R700 – R1,400 into a bigger one. Four public sources gathered in November 2026 disagree by roughly double on the same job. A drilling-company city guide puts Roodepoort at R350–R650 and Centurion at R420–R750 per metre. A separate cost guide says R700–R1,200 with R950 typical. A June 2026 company announcement cites R900–R1,400. An industry body figure quoted in the press puts the average near R600. None of these is our rate card. The spread exists because sellers quote high, guides quote wide, and nobody states what is included — so ask every quote what the metre rate covers.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry
- Confirm the stand's rated load against the full tank weight
- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration

Concentration decides the technology: low levels respond to simple filtration media, higher levels need oxidation before filtration, and very high levels need aeration and settling. Fitting a cartridge filter to water with serious iron just means changing a clogged brown cartridge every fortnight.

The orange staining on highveld borehole water, and what actually removes it.

- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration

- Ask whether a CoC is issued and who signs it

If you are pricing Greywater Systems in Linksfield, the number you want is Quoted per system on the fixtures collected and the irrigation served. That is a band, not a promise — but it is a real band, published up front, and it is close enough to budget against.

How that number is derived: Priced on which fixtures are collected and where the water goes. Greywater is genuinely useful and genuinely limited, and the limits are what most installers skip: it cannot be stored for long before it turns, it should go below the surface rather than onto leaves, and it is not suitable for every plant or every soil.

It is quoted per installation, which matters: two quotes on different bases are not comparable, however similar the rand figure looks.

Linksfield specifics. An established eastern Johannesburg suburb with freestanding houses on large stands and some townhouse and apartment developments. Housing here is mostly freestanding houses, townhouses and apartments, and that drives the final figure more than anything a call centre will tell you.

What we are actually talking about: Reusing bath and laundry water, within the limits that actually apply.

Where quotes go wrong

- A pressure pump sized for the tap, not for the house
- A tank stand built for a full tank's weight only on paper
- Treating borehole water for taste and ignoring the actual lab test

What to confirm before you pay anything

- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing
- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded
- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration
- Confirm the stand's rated load against the full tank weight
